title: Bauhaus and De Stijl
welcome_lead: Form follows function — and the grid follows logic.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: Bauhaus, De Stijl, and early modern design.

concepts.def: German school (1919-1933) uniting art, craft, industry.
Dutch designer (1888-1964), Red and Blue Chair 1917.
Belief that form should arise from function and material.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Bauhaus (1919, Weimar) under Gropius, then Hannes Meyer, then Mies van der Rohe, brought together painters, weavers, architects and metalworkers. Closed by Nazis in 1933; alumni scattered globally.

De Stijl (1917-1931), founded by Theo van Doesburg, advocated reduction to vertical and horizontal lines and primary colours. Rietveld's Red and Blue Chair (1917) and Schroder House (1924) translated the manifesto to objects.
Marcel Breuer's Wassily Chair (1925) used bent tubular steel — inspired by his bicycle frame — to redefine furniture industrially. Still in production today.
